messages:
anya: quick check-in on continuous-batcher handoff idea. thinking of a "cleanroom" boundary between admission and coalescer to decouple concerns. pros/cons?
luke: decoupling sounds good for modularity. main cons are potential extra copies and tracing gaps.
pat: copying adds mem pressure. we bench two modes: copy-handoff (safer) and pointer-handoff (faster). pointer reduces p50 but can spike p99 during GC.
anya: agreed. proposal: default copy-handoff for SLA tenants, pointer-handoff opt-in and gated behind a feature flag + per-tenant toggle.
luke: also propose a small lifecycle token when pointer-handoff used so buffers aren't freed. token is just an epoch/ref id emitted in traces.
pat: lifecycle token needs low overhead. prefer epoch-based reclamation: bump epoch on commit, GC reclaims older epochs.
infra-bot: note: deploy job queued for staging with feature-flag "batch.cleanroom" :rocket:
devx: observability note: emit minimal boundary events: `batch.handoff.{id,kind,origin_ts,hold_ms}` so SRE can stitch. keep tags low-cardinality (sla_bucket, kind).
anya: another mitigation: 3-way handshake (reserve/fill/commit). more messages but deterministic ownership and clearer backpressure.
luke: handshake also buys us an admission-level signal to refuse reserves under pressure.
pat: tradeoffs summary: copy-handoff = predictable tails, pointer = better median but tail risk, handshake = slightly higher protocol cost but deterministic GC and better telemetry.
anya: action items: pat will run microbench with epoch GC + pointer-handoff in staging, luke will draft per-tenant opt-in policy, i'll write a short RFC addendum with lifecycle tokens and required tracing events.
pat: will share perf numbers by EOW.
anya: thanks all. keeping this short
